nodes.label: Mind Your Tone: Investigating How Prompt Politeness Affects LLM Accuracy
nodes.author: Om Dobariya, Akhil Kumar
nodes.rationale: Investigates how prompt politeness/tone affects LLM accuracy on multiple-choice questions; finds impolite prompts outperform polite ones (84.8% vs 80.8%), contrary to prior work.

nodes.label: Five Politeness Levels
nodes.rationale: Spectrum from Very Polite to Very Rude; study creates 250 prompts (50 base questions × 5 variants) to systematically evaluate tone effects.

nodes.label: ChatGPT-4o Model
nodes.rationale: Primary model tested; shows accuracy range 80.8% (Very Polite) to 84.8% (Very Rude) with statistically significant differences (p<0.05).

nodes.label: Paired Sample T-Test Analysis
nodes.rationale: Statistical method used to assess significance of tone effects; 8 of 28 possible tone pairs show p-values < 0.05, indicating tone significantly affects accuracy.

nodes.label: Prior Work: Yin et al. (2024)
nodes.rationale: Prior study finding impolite prompts result in poor performance; current work partially contradicts this, suggesting newer LLMs respond differently to tone.

nodes.label: Perplexity as Explanatory Factor
nodes.rationale: Proposed explanation: lower perplexity prompts may perform better; politeness phrases may affect prompt perplexity independent of emotional content.
